title: Column-aligned text tables
instructions:
Implement `TextTable` in `text_table.py` for predictable plain-text reports.

## Files
- `text_table.py`

API:
- `TextTable(headers, alignments=None)`: `headers` is a list of one or more values,
  converted with `str`. Empty headers raise `ValueError`. `alignments` is either
  `None` (all columns left aligned), or a list with exactly one `"left"` or `"right"`
  per column. Wrong length or an unknown alignment raises `ValueError`.
- `add_row(values) -> None`: accept a list of exactly the header count, converting
  each value with `str`. A wrong count raises `ValueError` without adding a row.
- Headers and cells containing `\n` or `\r` raise `ValueError`. Invalid rows must
  leave the table unchanged. Copy input lists so later caller edits do not matter.
- `row_count() -> int`: number of data rows (not counting the header).
- `clear() -> None`: remove all data rows and retain headers and alignments.
- `render() -> str`: compute each column width as the maximum Python `len` of its
  header and current cells. Pad each cell with spaces on the appropriate side;
  headers use the same alignment as their column. Join columns with exactly
  `" | "`. The first line is the headers; the second joins runs of `-` of each
  column's width with `"-+-"`; subsequent lines are the rows in insertion order.
  Preserve padding, even at the end of a line. Join lines with `\n`, with no final
  newline. Always include the header and separator, even with zero rows. Empty
  cell strings are allowed, including a column with width zero.
